summary:
The slice changes only tests, as designed. Scanner.cs and the rest of src are byte-identical to b719e31.

What was built:
- LastAccessTests gains a three-row Theory (Offline, 0x80000, 0x100000). Each row asserts a listing precondition, Completed, Bytes 4 and Asked 3.
- LastAccessTests also gains a dedicated admin-share Fact (accepted m4), asserting Completed, Bytes 4 and (Asked, Kept) == (0, 0).
- The ContainerLayerStoreTests admin-share Fact asserts (Asked, Kept) == (0, 0) on `above` and on `throughLink`.
- The opt-in StalledShareTests asserts the same, still under Trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK.
- The committed driver tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/Mutants.ps1 discharges M1.

What I ran myself:
- The SL-102 acceptance repro: exit 0.
- The LastAccessTests and AScanThroughThisPcsAdminShare filter, under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp: all green both times.
- Mutants.ps1 -Temp Ordinary, all mutants: exit 0.
  - Unmutated: 874/874.
  - Mutant A: exactly the 3 Theory rows went red.
  - Mutant B: exactly the two admin-share Facts went red, so on this PC the share branch is really taken and the kill is not vacuous.
  - Each single-bit drop: only that bit's row went red.
  - Every run executed 874 tests, and every DLL was newer than its edit.
  - `git diff --exit-code src` was 0, the src digest was unchanged, and no copy or fsa-tests tree was left behind.
- Fitness op=check: all 91 rules hold.

How the driver is built:
- It fails rather than passing falsely: it requires the exact red set, the same executed count and the DLL timestamp.
- On a PC without admin shares, mutant B's empty red set makes the driver fail, so the vacuity the Facts' `continue` allows shows up there.

Declared deviations:
- `git ls-files` instead of `git archive`.
- Tuple asserts.
- The extra dedicated Fact.
- m5 not built, waived to SC-298.
- Design-record wording not edited.

All of them hold up against the code.

Findings: one, a minor extra. The new Fact re-implements ContainerLayerStoreTests' private Loopback path builder inline.

Not run: the SMB-LOOPBACK opt-in test. It is a person's check by design (New-SmbMapping changes machine state).

Second round: Second lens. I walked the changed code again looking for inputs it does not expect: Mutants.ps1's copier, matcher, TRX reader, path guard and digest; the Theory; the two share Facts; and the StalledShareTests assert.

Nothing in the C# tests breaks:
- SynchronousIoCancel.Created is [ThreadStatic], so the extra concurrent share scan cannot be captured by ContainerLayerStoreTests' WithGuard.
- No test mutates the OneDrive variables that ScanOptions.Default reads.
- A UNC, subst or no-admin-share TEMP lands in the already-filed silent-`continue` family (C-011).

In Mutants.ps1 the core checks fail safe rather than passing falsely:
- The old text must match exactly once, and a BOM is handled.
- The test DLL's timestamp must be newer than the edit.
- The executed counts must be equal and the red set must match exactly.
- No tracked file has a non-ASCII name, so git's output encoding cannot drop a file from the copy.

Two partial-failure paths the design did not list are filed as extras; neither sends the build back:
- A run killed before its `finally` leaves its copy, about 150 MB of build output plus sources, under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, and nothing sweeps it.
- The header says the src digest supports a run whose src is already dirty, but the closing `git diff --exit-code src` makes every such run exit 1, under a message that reads as worktree contamination.

findings.claim: LastAccessTests.NothingOnThisPcsAdminShareIsAskedToKeepItsLastAccessTime builds the admin-share path inline as `$@"\\{host}\{tree.Root[0]}$\{tree.Root[3..]}"`. That repeats character for character the private ContainerLayerStoreTests.Loopback helper (ContainerLayerStoreTests.cs:821). Both default-suite witnesses of M6's remote gate now carry their own copy of the local-path-to-admin-share rule. A fix to one, for example a TEMP root that is not a plain `X:\` path, can land in one copy and not the other. If the copies disagree, one Fact silently takes its `continue` branch and stops being a witness for mutant B, and nothing in the default suite would show it. Only Mutants.ps1, run by hand, would catch it.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LastAccessTests.cs (new Fact, the `share` line) and tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ContainerLayerStoreTests.cs:821 `private static string Loopback(string localPath, string host)`

quote.text: private static string Loopback(string localPath, string host) => $@"\\{host}\{localPath[0]}$\{localPath[3..]}";

findings.fix: Move Loopback into the shared Scans helper (for example `internal static string AdminShare(string localPath, string host)`) and call it from both Facts. The m4 decoupling from the workaround's test class still holds, because the helper would no longer belong to that class.

findings.claim: Mutants.ps1 deletes its copy only in the `finally` at :241-247. When the process is killed, that finally never runs: the engine's case runner kills at 120 s (Q-222), and a tool's 10-minute command cap can kill a run the build itself puts at 'about 10 minutes'. The copy is then left at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-sl102-mutants-<8hex>, holding about 1,000 source files plus the solution's bin/obj (149 MB measured in this worktree) and the TRX results. Nothing ever removes it, because each run makes a new random name and no run sweeps old ones. This repo has already recorded this leak shape: lesson #132 (851 fsa-* dirs) and Q-222 (about 140 folders per killed RuleCases pass).
findings.class_of: scratch roots left behind when a driver is killed before its finally
findings.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/Mutants.ps1:165 makes a fresh `fsa-sl102-mutants-<guid8>` per run; :241-247 is the only removal. Index line 93 tells validate to run it for about 10 minutes.
findings.fix: At startup, before making the new copy, remove any `fsa-sl102-mutants-*` folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp older than, say, 30 minutes, with [IO.Directory]::Delete and a logged note if one cannot go. Alternatively, write a marker naming the copy and delete it on the next run.

findings.claim: The comment above Get-SrcDigest says the digest 'shows nothing in the worktree changed even when src was already dirty at the start'. The closing check at :250-251 then runs `git diff --exit-code -- src`, which returns 1 whenever src has any unstaged edit, whether or not the driver caused it. So any run started with uncommitted src exits 1, and the FAIL line 'git diff --exit-code src returned 0' reports contamination that did not happen. One example is a later slice re-running the driver while it edits Scanner.cs near the gates, which is the same uncommitted-work case the declared `git ls-files` deviation was made for. Nothing passes falsely; the run just fails wrongly.

quote.text:
& git -C $Worktree diff --exit-code --stat -- src | Out-Null
Verify ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) 'git diff --exit-code src returned 0'

findings.fix: Capture `git -C $Worktree diff -- src` before the run, and at the end compare it with the same command's output instead of requiring exit 0. Keep exit 0 required only when the starting diff was empty. Otherwise drop the comment's claim.

obligations.evidence: I ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions.Tests.csproj`: 1/1 passed, exit 0. The repro file tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/LastAccessGatesAssertionsTests.cs is the repro stage's text and is unedited. It is owed to validate, but it holds now.

On this PC only. In my Mutants.ps1 run, mutant B turned both LastAccessTests.NothingOnThisPcsAdminShareIsAskedToKeepItsLastAccessTime and ContainerLayerStoreTests.AScanThroughThisPcsAdminShare... red, which shows the share branch was taken, the share reports NTFS and FileRemoteProtocolInfo succeeds. StalledShareTests.cs:18-19 remarks give the corrected reason: New-SmbMapping changes machine SMB mappings, and error 1312 occurs only under Windows Sandbox's SYSTEM. The design-record wording itself is outside the repo.

The Theory calls `TempTree.AddAttributes(tree.PathOf("off"), attribute)` (static) and asserts `Assert.Equal(attribute, (FileAttributes)Scans.Listing(tree.Root)["off"].Attributes & attribute)`. It compiles and passed in my runs.

The Theory's doc comment says the rows are literals not read from the mask, and that Pinned and Unpinned are numbers because System.IO.FileAttributes names neither. That is true: Kernel32.cs names both, and FileAttributes has no such members.

I ran the repro csproj against the edited tree: exit 0.

drift:
Mutants.ps1 differs from the design's mutant contract in three ways the build did not declare. None of them lets a mutant pass falsely.
- It runs `test tests\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --no-build` after one `build FsAnalyser.slnx --no-incremental` per mutant, not `test FsAnalyser.slnx` per TEMP. That is equivalent today, because Core.Tests is the only test project in the slnx.
- The design said a failure outside the expected set is re-run under both TEMPs before anyone calls it a regression. The driver does not re-run; it reports FAIL and lists what went red. A flake such as SynchronousIoCancelTests (lesson #127) therefore makes the driver exit 1, and a person must re-run it.

StalledShareTests puts the new assert at :114, after AssertChildrenAreContiguous as the design placed it. The design's reason, 'so a failure in an existing assertion is still reported first', does not fully hold: the existing `guard.ClosesHandedOff` assertion now comes after it.

Not a departure. The SMB-LOOPBACK assert (StalledShareTests.cs:114) has still never run in this tree. Only the spike's Sandbox measurement (asked 0 unmutated, 3 under B) exists, and it stays the person's check filed by the design.

Nothing new departed in this lens. The round-one drift notes stand. Mutants.ps1 tests the csproj with --no-build after one slnx build per mutant, does not re-run a failure outside the expected set, and StalledShareTests' new assert precedes the existing ClosesHandedOff assertion.
